**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred position met) — no redline proposed.**

Summary of the review:

- **Where a non-compete would live, none exists.** The restrictive-covenants article (§ X, p0124–p0125) contains only nondisclosure and a three-year employee **non-solicit** — a NONSOLICIT issue, deliberately not double-flagged under this rule.
- **Article II restrictions are licence-scope, not business restraints.** The "Field of Use" limit (p0007, p0030), the no-Derivative-Work bar (p0044), the third-party disclosure/training limits (p0041, p0042, p0045) and the sub-licence bar (Article VI, p0085) all govern how we may use *Licensor's* Licensed Technology. Nothing prevents us from buying, using or building another FX platform, or from competing with Licensor.
- **No exclusivity running against us.** The grant is expressly non-exclusive and Licensor may license others freely (p0043; preamble p0001), so Licensor retains no exclusive right that would block us from using or licensing our own product or brand — the condition that would otherwise defeat the preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" position.
- **Adjacent competition-flavoured terms belong to other rules.** The Change of Control clause allowing Licensor to withhold consent where the acquirer runs a competitive business (p0134) and the Right of First Refusal over a sale of our business (p0139) are change-of-control/assignment mechanics; they are commercially unattractive but are addressed under ASSIGN/change-of-control, not as a covenant limiting the businesses we may operate.

Since the preferred position is satisfied on the document's own terms, no redline was proposed and the fallback narrowing package was not needed.
